old: The second strand, blockchain-anchored records adapted to healthcare, has a deployed precedent in the Norwegian clinical context: the NewbornTime project. Brunner et al. (2025) document the deployment of a Hyperledger-based digital consent platform at Stavanger University Hospital, used between November 2021 and June 2025 in the collection of 1,012 thermal videos of newborn resuscitation events. The platform stores consent status immutably on-chain while keeping personal data encrypted and off-chain, providing a protected API for authorised retrieval and a documented General Data Protection Regulation-compliant withdrawal mechanism. The clinical viability of blockchain-anchored consent infrastructure in a Norwegian regulated healthcare setting is therefore established, although the system addresses consent recording rather than the audit-trail erasure problem.
A third strand applies zero-knowledge proofs
